items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training
4 - 7 years of related experience.
2 - 3 years of experience administering employee leave programs, preferably within a higher education or similarly complex organizational environment.
Experience with the University of California, Riverside's systems, policies, and procedures related to leave administration and leave management for staff and faculty.

Counsels employees on leave of absence process. Evaluates leave requests and medical certifications. Determines employee eligibility, calculates leave entitlement and provides information on benefits. (20% time)
Manages full range of cases in accordance with state and federal guidelines, University policy and collective bargaining agreements. (20% time)
Notifies managers of initial leave, return to work, and frequency and duration for intermittent leaves. May oversee timekeeping. (15% time)
Monitors leave ensuring receipt of relevant documentation, issues timely and accurate responses, and escalates requests extending beyond entitlement. (15% time)
Creates and updates cases in case/service management system(s). (10% time)
Coordinates with workers' compensation, disability management, benefits, and labor and employee relations. (5% time)
Documents trends in casework. Provides data and/or metrics as requested. (5% time)
Conducts LOA information sessions for managers and employees. (5% time)
Maintains thorough knowledge of FMLA/LOA, UC policies and procedures interpreting information for employees and managers. (5% time)
Read/Comprehend: Constantly
Write: Frequently
Perform Calculations: Frequently
Communicate Orally: Constantly
Reason & Analyze: Frequently
Sit: Constantly
Stand: Occasionally
Walk: Frequently
Thorough knowledge of FMLA, CFRA, PFL, PDL, Workers Comp, Military Leave, ERISA, HIPAA and applicable state and federal laws.
Knowledge of UCR human resources related systems such as UCPath, HRMS, ServiceNow.
Working knowledge of rules and regulations affecting employee benefit programs.
Knowledge of UC policies and UCR local procedures.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and safeguard information.
Knowledge and ability to apply Academic Personnel policies related to leaves of absence for Senate faculty, non-Senate academic appointees, and academic student employees.
Strong oral and written communication skills. Ability to communicate effectively and with confidence.
Knowledge of Collective Bargaining Agreements and their implications on leave laws, policies and procedures
Skill and sensitivity in dealing with others. Ability to handle difficult and complicated issues with professionalism and sound judgement.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
Ability to build relationships, collaborate and problem solve across all levels of the organization.
Critical thinking and problem solving skills.
Ability to provide high level of service and adapt to shifting priorities.
Knowledge of computer databases and Windows software.
